name: Sufjan Stevens
label: Asthmatic Kitty
lede: Sufjan Stevens announced an album for every US state, made two, and spent the next two decades doing everything else, nearly all of it on Asthmatic Kitty, the label he started with his stepfather, Lowell Brams. His latest, Javelin, was Pitchfork's No. 6 record of 2023.

eras.title: Born in Detroit, a label named after a cat
eras.text: Stevens grows up in northern Michigan on oboe and banjo, studies at Hope College, and in 1999 starts a record label with his stepfather. The name comes from a cat with asthma.

years.h: Sufjan Stevens is born in Detroit and raised in northern Michigan
years.p: The family moves to Alanson, Michigan, when he is nine. Interlochen Arts Academy and Hope College in Holland follow.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists a school run that includes Detroit Waldorf School, Alanson Public Schools, Interlochen Arts Academy and Harbor Light Christian School. He graduated from Hope College Phi Beta Kappa, and later earned an MFA in creative writing from The New School in New York.

years.h: At Hope College he joins two bands and plays with Danielson
years.p: Marzuki is a folk-rock band, Con Los Dudes a garage outfit. The Danielson Famile is the connection that lasts.
years.xp: Stevens keeps the Danielson link for years. In his last semester at Hope he records what becomes his first solo album, A Sun Came.

years.src: Wikipedia: Asthmatic Kitty · Wikipedia: Sufjan Stevens
years.h: A cat with asthma gives Asthmatic Kitty its name
years.p: Sara was a stray that Lowell Brams adopted in 1994. In 1999 he and his stepson Sufjan Stevens start the label in Holland, Michigan.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Asthmatic Kitty was founded by a community of musicians from Holland, Michigan, led by Stevens and [[Lowell Brams|4133fffc-c180-464e-b901-221b9c7e8c06]]. Sara's symptoms eased after Brams moved to Lander, Wyoming, in 2002, thanks to the altitude and dry air. She died in December 2008, around fifteen or sixteen years old.

The label is now based in Bloomington, Indiana, and releases nearly everything Stevens makes for the next quarter century.

years.h: He plays fourteen instruments on A Sun Came
years.p: Mostly recorded in Holland in 1998 on a four-track, with banjo, sitar, oboe and xylophone in the mix.
years.xp: Stevens described the sound himself as traditional pop, medieval instrumentation with Middle Eastern inflections, tape loops, digital samples, manic percussion and Arabic chants. Marzuki Stevens plays guitar, percussion and saxophone, and Shannon Stephens sings on a few tracks.

eras.title: A banjo, an oboe and a promise of fifty albums
eras.text: Two records in, Stevens announces an album for every US state. The banjo and the state pride win him an audience, and the plan itself turns out to be more brand than blueprint.

years.h: Enjoy Your Rabbit sets the Chinese zodiac to electronics
years.p: A song cycle built on the animals of the zodiac, a long way from the banjo records that follow it.
years.xp: It tells you the banjo was never the whole plan. Stevens comes back to synths and drum machines on The Age of Adz nine years later.

years.h: He writes his home state a record, Michigan
years.p: Recorded with two Shure SM57s and an AKG C1000 in places like Petoskey and Brooklyn. Pitchfork gave it 8.5.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Brandon Stosuy called it a beautiful, sprawling homage, and noted some tracks ran long. By 2005 it had sold 27,000 copies in the US, according to Wikipedia. The cover is hand-painted by Laura Normandin, a crafts editor at Martha Stewart Living.

Its song "Redford" would later inspire the title and structure of The Roots' 2011 album.

q: Sufjan Stevens, as summarized by Wikipedia
years.h: After Michigan, he promises fifty states and delivers one more
years.p: Illinois is the only other state album he ever makes.
years.xp: Stevens later acknowledged the fifty-states pitch was a promotional gimmick he never seriously planned to finish, according to Wikipedia. The stunt worked anyway: it handed a banjo-and-oboe folk musician a story journalists could not resist.

years.h: Seven Swans points the banjo at Abraham and the Transfiguration
years.p: Recorded at Daniel Smith's home studio and the New Jerusalem Rec Room in Clarksboro, NJ. Pitchfork gave it 8.1.
years.xp: The Guardian called it a record of remarkable delicacy, and Spin described it as Elliott Smith after ten years of Sunday school. It came out on Sounds Familyre, and Asthmatic Kitty reissued it in 2016.

eras.title: Illinois makes him, and he builds an orchestra to tour it
eras.text: The breakthrough arrives with 22 tracks and titles that read like footnotes. He takes a band of strings and singers on the road, boxes up five discs of Christmas songs and sells out a Brooklyn opera house.

years.cap: Stevens and the Illinoisemakers on the Illinois tour, September 9, 2005
years.h: Illinois has 22 tracks and a UFO sighting near Highland
years.p: Recorded in Queens and around New York. Pitchfork gave it 9.2 and later placed it No. 16 on its 2000s list.
years.xp:
Most of it was cut between late 2004 and January 2005 at The Buddy Project in Astoria, Queens, and the whole thing runs 73:59. The titles include "Concerning the UFO Sighting Near Highland, Illinois" and "The Predatory Wasp of the Palisades Is Out to Get Us!". Pitchfork called the record "strange and lush, as excessive and challenging as its giant, gushing song titles."

Metacritic scores it 90/100. It is Stevens's first Billboard 200 entry, peaking at No. 121, and the RIAA certified it Gold in 2017. It also includes "John Wayne Gacy, Jr.", a song about the Chicago serial killer.

The original cover shows Superman, and DC Comics objected: later pressings swap in a balloon sticker, and early copies reportedly sold for up to $75 on eBay. His live band, the Illinoisemakers, is eight to ten string players and singers.

years.h: "Chicago" keeps getting licensed
years.p: It lands in Little Miss Sunshine, Veronica Mars, The Politician and, as a demo, The Bear.
years.xp: Stevens cut five versions, including an acoustic take and an arrangement he labeled Adult Contemporary Easy Listening. The RIAA has certified it Gold, and Pitchfork put it in The Pitchfork 500.

years.h: Songs for Christmas boxes up five years of holiday recordings
years.p: He recorded a set annually from 2001, skipping 2004, as an exercise in learning to appreciate the holiday. Original carols and standards fill the five discs.
years.xp: He follows it with Silver & Gold in 2012, 58 more songs, bringing the total to 100 Christmas tracks. That year's tour is billed as the "Sirfjam Stephanapolous Christmas Sing-a-Long Seasonal Affective Disorder Spectacular Music Pageant Variety Show Disaster."

years.h: No advertising, and The BQE still sells out the BAM Opera House
years.p: The house seats 2,109. The piece is a 30-minute symphonic tribute to Brooklyn's expressway, with 36 performers, hula hoopers and a Super 8 film he shot himself.
years.xp: Wikipedia says it sold out with no advertising. It later won the 2008 Brendan Gill Prize.

eras.title: Glitch, a virus and a lot of side projects
eras.text: Stevens swaps the banjo for synths and drum machines, a 25-minute closer included, then spends the next years on collaborations. In 2012 his mother dies.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Age of Adz · Wikipedia: Sufjan Stevens
years.h: The Age of Adz drops the banjo for glitch and hip-hop beats
years.p: Royal Robertson, an outsider artist, inspires it, and the closer, "Impossible Soul", runs 25 minutes. Pitchfork gave it 8.4.
years.xp:
Stevens said a mysterious, debilitating virus that affected his nervous system in 2009 and 2010 shaped the record: "That's why I think the record's really obsessed with sensation." It debuted at No. 7 on the Billboard 200 with 36,000 copies, his best opening at that time, per Wikipedia.

Metacritic scores it 80/100, and reviewers split on "Impossible Soul", some praising its ideas and others calling it bloated. The All Delighted People EP had arrived on August 20, and reached No. 27 on the Billboard 200 on digital sales alone.

years.h: Son Lux and Serengeti join him for Beak & Claw
years.p: S/S/S, a three-way EP on Anticon and the first of two rounds with the trio.

years.h: His mother, Carrie, dies of stomach cancer
years.p: She had left the family when he was an infant. The record about her, Carrie & Lowell, follows in 2015.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports that Carrie struggled with depression, schizophrenia and substance abuse. In the years that followed Stevens turned the loss into the songs on his 2015 record, which opens with "Death With Dignity".

eras.title: A record about grief, then a red carpet
eras.text: Carrie & Lowell is the quietest record he has made and the one everybody ends up talking about. Two years later a movie soundtrack puts him on the Oscars stage.

years.src: Wikipedia: Carrie & Lowell · Stereogum: Carrie & Lowell Turns 10
years.h: His mother's death becomes Carrie & Lowell
years.p: Recorded across Brooklyn, Portland, Oklahoma, Wisconsin and a Klamath Falls hotel room on an iPhone. Pitchfork gave it 9.3.
years.xp:
Producer Thomas Bartlett (Doveman) shaped the sparse sound. "Thomas took all these sketches and made sense of it all," Stevens said. "He called me out on my bullshit." Of the recording itself: "I was recording songs as a means of grieving, making sense of it. But the writing and recording wasn't the salve I expected."

It debuted at No. 10 on the Billboard 200 with 53,000 equivalent units, and had sold 105,000 by July 2015, nearly half of them on vinyl. Pitchfork ranked it No. 6 for 2015, and raised its own score to 10 for the 10th anniversary, according to Wikipedia. Stereogum put it 16th on its decade list.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mystery of Love · The Fader: Watch Sufjan Stevens perform Mystery Of Love at the Oscars
years.h: Stevens takes the Oscars stage in a dragon-embossed tuxedo
years.p: Chris Thile, Moses Sumney and St. Vincent back him on "Mystery of Love", which loses to "Remember Me" from Coco.
years.xp:
Director Luca Guadagnino first asked Stevens to narrate Call Me by Your Name. Stevens declined and offered original music instead, with full creative control. The soundtrack came out on December 1, 2017, with "Mystery of Love", "Visions of Gideon" and a piano version of "Futile Devices". Guadagnino wanted music that could "give the film a precise identity."

The tuxedo was Gucci, pink and purple stripes with blue dragons, and his first. He earned a Grammy nomination, won Italy's David di Donatello for the song in 2019, and the song has gone platinum in the US, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: Stevens at the Pitchfork Music Festival
years.h: Planetarium finally gets a studio recording
years.p: Eighty minutes with Bryce Dessner, Nico Muhly and James McAlister, five years after the live project began.

eras.title: Ambient, and a lot of it
eras.text: He makes an ambient record with his stepfather, an 80-minute one alone, and a concept album drawn from films with a friend, all on his own label.

years.h: He and Lowell Brams go ambient on Aporia
years.p: Twenty-one tracks that mix organic instrumentation with experimental electronics, new age and ambient.

years.h: The Ascension runs 80 minutes, and "America" alone takes 12
years.p: He plays, records, arranges and mixes it himself, with Casey Foubert and Bryce Dessner on guitar. Pitchfork gave it a 7.0.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Sam Sodomsky called it kind of a drag. The New York Times put it No. 1 on its best albums of 2020 list, per Wikipedia, and Exclaim! gave it 10/10.

years.h: Angelo De Augustine joins him for A Beginner's Mind
years.p: A concept album drawn from films of the 20th and 21st centuries.

eras.title: Loss, an illness and a quiet album
eras.text: Evans Richardson dies in April, Stevens is diagnosed with Guillain-Barré, and he returns to the singer-songwriter mode of Carrie & Lowell.

years.big: "the light of my life, my beloved partner and best friend"
q: the light of my life, my beloved partner and best friend
Sufjan Stevens, dedicating Javelin to Evans Richardson
years.h: Evans Richardson, his partner, dies in April
years.p: Stevens dedicates Javelin to Richardson on release day.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the dedication as the first time Stevens had publicly discussed Evans Richardson or his own sexuality. Richardson worked as chief of staff at the Studio Museum in Harlem and had been elected chair of the American Alliance of Museums accreditation commission in 2021.

years.h: "So You Are Tired" is the first Javelin single
years.p: It arrives with the album announcement, scaled-down and acoustic, the first sign he is heading back toward Carrie & Lowell.

years.h: Stevens says Guillain-Barré has him relearning to walk
years.p: He tells fans in September that he is in physical rehabilitation, a few weeks before Javelin comes out.

years.src: Wikipedia: Javelin (album) · Album of the Year: Sufjan Stevens - Javelin
years.h: Javelin brings him back to full singer-songwriter mode
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.6, Best New Music, and ranked it No. 6 of 2023.
years.xp:
He recorded most of it alone at home, with Hannah Cohen, Megan Lui, Nedelle Torrisi and Adrienne Maree Brown singing and [[Bryce Dessner|20336142-85de-4e11-a1fd-a6c815b4e583]] on guitar. It has nine originals and a Neil Young cover, "There's a World", plus a track with baroque recorders, "My Red Little Fox". A 48-page art book with ten essays shipped with it.

Metacritic lists it at 87/100, and Album of the Year's critics average is 88. It peaked at No. 30 on the Billboard 200, with 4,335 US units in its first week, and No. 7 in the UK.

eras.title: Illinoise goes to Broadway
eras.text: Nearly twenty years on, the album that made his name becomes a dance musical.

years.cap: Illinoise cast members greeting fans at the stage door after the Broadway opening, April 24, 2024
years.src: Wikipedia: Sufjan Stevens · Wikipedia: Illinois (Sufjan Stevens album)
years.h: A dance show built on Illinois opens in Chicago, then Broadway
years.p: Justin Peck directs and choreographs. It opens at Chicago Shakespeare Theater, then plays the St. James Theatre April 24 to August 10.
years.xp: Story credit goes to Peck and Jackie Sibblies Drury, with Timo Andres handling orchestrations. It earned four Tony nominations, including Best Musical, and won Best Choreography for Peck.
